outlines.paper_title: A Comprehensive Survey on Multimodal RAG: All Combinations of Modalities as Input and Output
outlines.outline_pattern: Taxonomy-driven followed by a process-oriented workflow analysis

sections.title: Introduction
sections.description: Introduces the evolution of Large Language Models (LLMs) to Multimodal LLMs (MLLMs) and the necessity of Multimodal RAG (MM-RAG) to mitigate hallucinations. It highlights the limitations of existing surveys, presents the paper's unique contribution (covering all modality combinations), and outlines the paper's structure.

sections.title: Problem Formulation
sections.description: Provides the mathematical definition of the MM-RAG framework. It defines the three core components: the Knowledge Base (D), the Retriever (R), and the Generator (G), and formulates the optimization objective of minimizing the difference between generated output and ground truth.

sections.title: Taxonomy
sections.description: Presents a comprehensive taxonomy matrix based on 54 possible input-output modality combinations. It analyzes existing work within these combinations and identifies unexplored areas.

subsections.title: Input
subsections.description: Analyzes encoders and processing methods for various input modalities used to query the knowledge base.

subsections.title: Text
subsections.description: Discusses text as the basic modality for retrieval, using models like BERT and T5.

subsections.title: Image
subsections.description: Covers image inputs using encoders like ViT, ResNet, and Vision-Language Models (CLIP, BLIP) for alignment.

subsections.title: Audio
subsections.description: Examines audio inputs using models like Wav2vec, HuBERT, and CLAP.

subsections.title: Video
subsections.description: Discusses video inputs, utilizing Large Video Language Models or converting video to text/images for processing.

subsections.title: Code
subsections.description: Reviews code as a modality, using specialized encoders like CodeT5 and GraphCodeBERT.

subsections.title: Structured Data
subsections.description: Discusses knowledge graphs and tables as inputs for tasks like KBQA and Table QA.

subsections.title: Others
subsections.description: Briefly touches on other modalities like time-series data forecasting.

subsections.title: Output
subsections.description: Analyzes the generation capabilities for different output modalities based on retrieved information.

subsections.title: Text
subsections.description: Covers text generation from multimodal inputs (e.g., image captioning, VQA) using LLMs and MLLMs.

subsections.title: Image
subsections.description: Discusses image generation using GANs, diffusion models, and VLMs augmented by retrieval.

subsections.title: Audio
subsections.description: Reviews audio generation (TTS, music) using spectral generation or large audio models.

subsections.title: Video
subsections.description: Discusses the nascent field of RAG-based video generation using diffusion models.

subsections.title: 3D data
subsections.description: Covers text-to-3D generation using retrieved 3D assets or motion samples.

subsections.title: Code
subsections.description: Examines code generation and completion using retrieved documentation and snippets.

subsections.title: Insights from the Taxonomy
subsections.description: Summarizes the findings from the taxonomy matrix, highlighting empty cells as opportunities for future research and summarizing common models for core components.

sections.title: Workflow
sections.description: Deconstructs the MM-RAG system into four essential operational stages: Pre-retrieval, Retrieval, Augmentation, and Generation.

subsections.title: Pre-Retrieval
subsections.description: Focuses on preparing the data and the query before the actual search occurs.

subsections.title: Knowledge Base Preparation
subsections.description: Details data preprocessing, chunking, and organization methods (Uni-modal Embedding, Pair-wise Storage, Unified Embedding, Graph Construction).

subsections.title: Query Preparation
subsections.description: Discusses techniques to refine inputs: Query Expansion, Rewriting, Transformation, Dropout, and Multi-Query strategies.

subsections.title: Retrieval
subsections.description: Analyzes the core retrieval mechanisms used to fetch relevant documents.

subsections.title: Retriever
subsections.description: Compares Sparse Retrievers (BM25), Dense Retrievers (CLIP, DPR), and other specialized retrievers.

subsections.title: Retrieval Strategy
subsections.description: Reviews strategies like Hybrid Retrieval and Hierarchical Retrieval.

subsections.title: Retrieval Timing
subsections.description: Discusses when retrieval occurs: Single, Iterative, or Adaptive Retrieval.

subsections.title: Augmentation
subsections.description: Describes how retrieved data is processed before being fed to the generator.

subsections.title: Context Reranking
subsections.description: Re-scoring retrieved documents to improve precision.

subsections.title: Context Selection
subsections.description: Filtering irrelevant or redundant information.

subsections.title: Context Compression
subsections.description: Reducing dimensionality or size of embeddings to fit context windows.

subsections.title: Noise Injection
subsections.description: Adding noise during training to improve model robustness.

subsections.title: Context Fusion
subsections.description: Methods to integrate query and documents: Fusion by Concatenation (FiE, FiD) and Fusion by Latent Aggregation.

subsections.title: Generation
subsections.description: Details the generator architecture (Modality Encoder, Projectors, LLM Backbone, Modality Generator).

subsections.title: Enhancement Approaches
subsections.description: Discusses Prompt Engineering and MLLM Fine-tuning to improve generation quality.

sections.title: Training Strategies
sections.description: Categorizes approaches for training MM-RAG systems based on parameter updates.

subsections.title: Parameter-Frozen Strategies
subsections.description: Discusses using off-the-shelf models without fine-tuning to reduce costs.

subsections.title: Parameter-Trainable Strategies
subsections.description: Covers methods that update model parameters for better alignment.

subsections.title: Modular Training
subsections.description: Independent optimization of components (Retriever, Generator, Extra Layers).

subsections.title: End-to-end Training
subsections.description: Joint training of retriever and generator for holistic optimization.

sections.title: Evaluation and Benchmarks
sections.description: Discusses metrics and methods for assessing MM-RAG performance.

subsections.title: Evaluation of the Retriever
subsections.description: Focuses on Retrieval Relevance and Retrieval Quality metrics.

sections.title: Applications
sections.description: Discusses various applications of MM-RAG (inferred from Introduction roadmap).

sections.title: Future Directions
sections.description: Explores future research opportunities in the field (inferred from Introduction roadmap).

sections.title: Conclusion
sections.description: Concluding remarks (inferred from Introduction roadmap).

structural_insights.organization_logic: The paper follows a classic engineering survey structure: Definition -> Taxonomy (What) -> Workflow (How) -> Training (Build) -> Evaluation (Measure). This logical flow allows readers to first understand the landscape before diving into technical implementation details.
structural_insights.transition_strategy: The paper uses the Taxonomy Matrix (Table 1) as a central pivot. It first defines the matrix to categorize existing literature, then uses the specific modality combinations identified in the matrix to structure the detailed technical discussions in the subsequent sections.
structural_insights.depth_analysis: The paper shows significant depth in the 'Workflow' section (Section 4), breaking it down into four distinct stages with multiple sub-strategies. This contrasts with the 'Taxonomy' section which is broad but shallower, serving as an index. The inclusion of 'Pre-retrieval' and 'Augmentation' adds necessary granularity often missed in simpler RAG surveys.
key_strengths: Comprehensive Taxonomy Matrix covering 54 input-output combinations.
Clear separation of the RAG workflow into four distinct, actionable stages.
Detailed breakdown of specific encoders and generators for every modality type.
Structured comparison of training strategies (Frozen vs. Trainable).

outlines.paper_title: Advances in Feed-Forward 3D Reconstruction and View Synthesis: A Survey
outlines.paper_topic: Feed-forward methods for 3D reconstruction and novel view synthesis using deep learning
outlines.outline_pattern: Taxonomy-based organization centered on underlying 3D representations, followed by downstream applications and evaluation benchmarks.

sections.title: Introduction
sections.description: Introduces the shift from traditional optimization-based methods (like SfM and standard NeRF) to feed-forward learning-based approaches. It outlines the motivation for faster inference and better generalization, defines the scope (post-NeRF era), and presents the survey's categorization strategy based on scene representations (NeRF, Pointmap, 3DGS, etc.).

sections.title: Methods
sections.description: The core technical section categorizing feed-forward approaches based on their underlying scene representations. It details how neural networks infer 3D structure or novel views in a single forward pass without per-scene optimization.

subsections.title: NeRF
subsections.description: Reviews methods that infer Neural Radiance Fields directly from input images. These approaches eliminate per-scene optimization by learning to predict density and color from learned features.

subsections.title: 1D Feature-based Methods
subsections.description: Discusses methods that encode the scene into a global 1D latent code shared by all 3D points, often disentangling shape and appearance.

subsections.title: 2D Feature-based Methods
subsections.description: Covers approaches using image encoders to extract pixel-aligned features, which are then aggregated via ray projection or transformers to guide NeRF prediction.

subsections.title: 3D Feature-based Methods
subsections.description: Examines methods utilizing explicit 3D structures like cost volumes (MVS-based) or triplanes (LRM-based) to store geometric and appearance features for volumetric rendering.

subsections.title: Other Methods
subsections.description: Briefly mentions alternative feature integration strategies, such as Vision Transformers and Multiplane Images (MPI), for feed-forward NeRF reconstruction.

subsections.title: Pointmap
subsections.description: Focuses on methods that directly regress pixel-aligned 3D pointmaps (e.g., DUSt3R, MASt3R). It covers architectures for stereo and multiview reconstruction, memory mechanisms for sequential processing, and foundation models for 3D geometry.

subsections.title: 3DGS
subsections.description: Reviews feed-forward methods predicting 3D Gaussian Splatting parameters. This section highlights the efficiency of rasterization-based approaches compared to volumetric rendering.

subsections.title: Gaussian Map
subsections.description: Discusses methods predicting 2D maps where pixels correspond to 3D Gaussians. Includes epipolar-based, cost volume-based, and pre-trained reconstruction model approaches.

subsections.title: Gaussian Volume
subsections.description: Covers methods representing scenes as Gaussian voxel grids or triplanes, enabling implicit feature matching and progressive reconstruction for complex scenes.

subsections.title: Other 3D Representations
subsections.description: Surveys feed-forward reconstruction using traditional or implicit representations other than NeRF or Gaussians.

subsections.title: Mesh
subsections.description: Reviews methods generating explicit mesh topology, including diffusion-based generation and Large Reconstruction Models (LRMs) for meshes.

subsections.title: Occupancy
subsections.description: Discusses methods predicting occupancy probabilities to define inside/outside status of 3D points.

subsections.title: SDF
subsections.description: Examines methods predicting Signed Distance Functions, often utilizing MVS or transformer-based architectures for surface reconstruction.

subsections.title: 3D-Free Models
subsections.description: Analyzes approaches that synthesize novel views directly without explicit 3D representations.

subsections.title: Regression-based View Synthesis
subsections.description: Covers transformer-based models (like SRT) that regress target pixel colors from source views via latent representations.

subsections.title: Generative View Synthesis
subsections.description: Discusses generative models, particularly image and video diffusion models, used to hallucinate novel views and ensure multiview consistency.

sections.title: Tasks & Applications
sections.description: Explores the diverse downstream applications enabled by feed-forward models, ranging from fundamental vision tasks to complex robotics and generation scenarios.

subsections.title: Camera Pose Estimation
subsections.description: Discusses how feed-forward models (especially pointmap-based) allow for direct estimation of camera intrinsics and extrinsics without traditional SfM pipelines.

subsections.title: Pose-Free 3D Reconstruction & View Synthesis
subsections.description: Reviews methods capable of reconstructing scenes or objects from unposed images, handling the joint optimization of geometry and camera parameters.

subsections.title: Dynamic 3D Reconstruction & View Synthesis
subsections.description: Covers the challenging task of reconstructing moving scenes (4D), involving dynamic object segmentation and temporal consistency handling.

subsections.title: Image Matching
subsections.description: Highlights how feed-forward reconstruction models (like MASt3R) serve as robust dense feature matchers for stereo and multiview tasks.

subsections.title: 3D-Aware Image Synthesis
subsections.description: Examines generative models (GANs and Diffusion) that incorporate 3D representations to synthesize consistent images from novel viewpoints.

subsections.title: Camera-Controlled Video Generation
subsections.description: Discusses video generation models that allow explicit control over camera trajectories using 3D priors or point clouds.

subsections.title: 3D Understanding
subsections.description: Reviews methods embedding semantic features into reconstruction models for tasks like segmentation and Visual Question Answering (3D-VQA).

subsections.title: Digital Human
subsections.description: Briefly touches upon generating photorealistic, animatable 3D avatars using feed-forward Gaussian or NeRF models.

subsections.title: SLAM & Visual Localization
subsections.description: Explores the integration of feed-forward models into real-time SLAM systems to replace traditional geometric pipelines.

subsections.title: Robot Manipulation
subsections.description: Mentions the emerging use of generalizable NeRF and 3DGS models for robotic grasping and manipulation tasks.

sections.title: Evaluation
sections.description: Provides a comprehensive overview of the resources and metrics used to benchmark feed-forward methods.

subsections.title: Datasets
subsections.description: Tabulates and describes popular datasets (synthetic and real, static and dynamic) used for training and testing.

subsections.title: Evaluation Metrics
subsections.description: Definitions of standard metrics for view synthesis (PSNR, SSIM), pose estimation (RTA, RRA), and geometry (Chamfer distance, Depth accuracy).

subsections.title: Evaluation Results
subsections.description: Summarizes quantitative performance of state-of-the-art methods across various benchmarks for pose, point maps, depth, and view synthesis.

sections.title: Open Challenges
sections.description: Discusses remaining hurdles in the field, such as limited modality diversity, generalization issues, and computational costs (Note: Content is truncated in source).

structural_insights.organization_logic: The paper follows a classic survey structure: Introduction -> Taxonomy of Methods (organized by 3D representation type) -> Applications -> Evaluation Resources -> Future Directions. This allows readers to first understand the 'how' (architecture) before the 'what' (applications).
structural_insights.transition_strategy: The transition from Methods (Section 2) to Applications (Section 3) is logical, moving from core algorithmic designs to their practical utility. The separation of 'Methods' by representation (NeRF vs. Pointmap vs. 3DGS) reflects the current fragmentation and evolution of the field.
structural_insights.depth_analysis: The 'Methods' section is highly granular, breaking down NeRF and 3DGS into specific feature-integration strategies. This depth is balanced by a broad 'Applications' section that demonstrates the versatility of these methods beyond simple reconstruction.
key_strengths: Clear taxonomy based on underlying 3D representations (NeRF, Pointmap, 3DGS, Mesh, 3D-free).
Detailed breakdown of emerging 'Pointmap' methods (DUSt3R lineage), which is a very recent trend.
Extensive coverage of downstream applications beyond just view synthesis, including Robotics and SLAM.
Comprehensive tabulation of datasets and quantitative comparison of recent SOTA methods.

outlines.paper_title: Reinforcement Learning Meets Large Language Models: A Survey of Advancements and Applications Across the LLM Lifecycle
outlines.paper_topic: Reinforcement Learning (RL) application in Large Language Models (LLMs), focusing on the full lifecycle from pre-training to alignment and reasoning (RLVR).

sections.title: Introduction
sections.description: Introduces the rise of LLMs and the necessity of RL for alignment and reasoning. It highlights the shift from standard RLHF to Reinforcement Learning with Verifiable Rewards (RLVR) exemplified by models like DeepSeek-R1 and OpenAI-o1. It outlines the survey's goal to cover the full RL lifecycle.

subsections.title: Related Surveys
subsections.description: Reviews existing surveys, noting their limitations such as narrow focus on alignment or lack of lifecycle coverage. It positions this survey as a comprehensive review covering pre-training, alignment, and the latest inference-time reasoning advancements.

subsections.title: Contribution Summary
subsections.description: Summarizes the paper's three main contributions: a lifecycle-based organization of RL methods, a focus on advanced RLVR technology, and a consolidation of resources including datasets, benchmarks, and frameworks.

sections.title: Preliminaries of Reinforcement Learning
sections.description: Establishes the theoretical foundations of RL, modeling the problem as a Markov Decision Process (MDP). It distinguishes between the two primary paradigms used in LLM training: policy-based learning and value-based learning.

subsections.title: Policy Learning
subsections.description: Details methods that directly optimize the policy, including REINFORCE, Actor-Critic, TRPO, and PPO. It specifically highlights Group Relative Policy Optimization (GRPO), a key algorithm for reasoning models that eliminates the value network to save resources.

subsections.title: Value Learning
subsections.description: Explains methods that estimate value functions to derive policies, such as Q-learning, SARSA, and DQN. It notes that while less common in direct LLM generation due to action space size, these concepts influence specific techniques like exemplar selection.

sections.title: Reinforcement Learning Methods in the Pre-training Phase and Alignment Phase
sections.description: Reviews the application of RL in the early stages of the LLM lifecycle. It covers attempts to integrate RL into pre-training and details the established methods used for aligning models with human preferences.

subsections.title: Reinforcement Learning Methods in the Pre-training Phase
subsections.description: Discusses niche approaches to introducing RL during pre-training, such as reconstructing next-token prediction as a reasoning task, visual pre-training with RL, and 'mid-training' strategies to prepare models for RL scaling.

subsections.title: Classic Algorithms in the Alignment Phase
subsections.description: Summarizes standard alignment techniques including RLHF, Constitutional AI, RLAIF, and Direct Preference Optimization (DPO). It touches on methods for mitigating reward hacking and optimizing for human utility.

subsections.title: Emerging Methods for Reward Model Design
subsections.description: Focuses on innovations in reward modeling, such as Reward Reasoning Models (RRM) that use Chain-of-Thought, generative process reward models, and rule-based rewards to improve the accuracy and generalization of feedback signals.

sections.title: Reinforcement Learning Methods in the Reasoning Phase
sections.description: The core section of the survey, focusing on RL with Verifiable Rewards (RLVR). It explores how RL is used to enhance complex reasoning in math, code, and multimodal tasks, analyzing algorithms, experimental findings, and adaptive strategies.

subsections.title: Experimental Findings of RLVR in Improving the Reasoning Ability of LLMs
subsections.description: Analyzes whether RLVR truly creates new reasoning capabilities or merely acts as an efficient sampler. It discusses the 'entropy collapse' phenomenon, the necessity of explicit thinking processes, and the boundaries of model capability.

subsections.title: Recent Advances in RL Algorithms for LLMs
subsections.description: Chronicles the latest algorithms post-2024, including improvements to GRPO, DAPO for long sequences, Open-Reasoner-Zero, and various hybrid strategies combining SFT and RL to stabilize training and improve efficiency.

subsections.title: Application of RLVR in Multimodal Reasoning
subsections.description: Examines the application of RLVR to Vision-Language Models (VLMs), video reasoning, and embodied intelligence. It covers specific models like Vision-R1 and techniques for visual generation and spatial reasoning.

subsections.title: Adaptive Reasoning
subsections.description: Discusses methods to control the length and depth of Chain-of-Thought reasoning. It covers 'budget forcing', thinking mode switching (long vs. short), and difficulty-aware resource allocation during inference.

subsections.title: RLVR for Agent
subsections.description: Addresses the challenges of applying RL to multi-turn agents, such as delayed rewards and long horizons. It reviews frameworks for tool use, memory management, and environment interaction (e.g., Minecraft, web search).

subsections.title: Reinforcement Learning from Internal Feedback
subsections.description: Explores unsupervised or self-supervised RL methods that rely on internal signals like self-certainty or consistency rather than external labels, aiming to activate pre-trained knowledge without human supervision.

sections.title: Datasets and Benchmarks
sections.description: Surveys the data resources required for RL training and evaluation. It categorizes resources into synthetic data generation pipelines and established benchmarks for various domains.

subsections.title: Synthetic Data Generation
subsections.description: Describes frameworks for generating training data without human annotation, including methods for creating reasoning chains, tool-use trajectories, and difficulty-adapted questions to support RLVR.

subsections.title: Datasets and Benchmarks
subsections.description: Lists and categorizes standard benchmarks for alignment (e.g., HHH, HH-RLHF), code (APPS, SWE-bench), math (GSM8K, MATH), and general knowledge, used to evaluate RL-enhanced models.

structural_insights.organization_logic: The paper follows the chronological lifecycle of an LLM. It begins with theoretical foundations, moves to Pre-training (early stage), then Alignment (standard post-training), and culminates in Reasoning (the current frontier/late-stage post-training). It concludes with the necessary supporting resources (Data/Benchmarks).
structural_insights.transition_strategy: The transition is evolutionary. Section 3 covers the 'classic' RLHF era (Alignment), while Section 4 transitions to the 'modern' RLVR era (Reasoning), reflecting the industry's shift from making models 'safe' to making them 'smart'.
structural_insights.depth_analysis: The structure is heavily weighted towards Section 4 (Reasoning), which contains 6 subsections. This reflects the survey's focus on the most recent advancements (2024-2025) like DeepSeek-R1 and o1. Sections 2 and 3 provide necessary context but are less granular than the reasoning section.
key_strengths: Clear separation of 'Alignment' and 'Reasoning' phases, which clarifies the evolving role of RL.
Inclusion of a specific subsection on 'Experimental Findings' (4.1) which discusses the *nature* of intelligence emergence, not just algorithms.
Comprehensive taxonomy (referenced in text) that maps algorithms to specific lifecycle stages.
Timeliness: Dedicated focus on RLVR and GRPO, which are the immediate state-of-the-art techniques.

outlines.paper_title: Vision-Language-Action Models for Autonomous Driving: Past, Present, and Future
outlines.paper_topic: Autonomous Driving, specifically the evolution from Vision-Action (VA) to Vision-Language-Action (VLA) models

sections.title: Introduction
sections.description: Introduces the limitations of traditional modular and Vision-Action (VA) pipelines, motivates the shift to Vision-Language-Action (VLA) models enabled by LLMs, and outlines the paper's contributions and structure.

sections.title: Preliminary Foundations
sections.description: Formalizes the general formulation of VLA models and details their three core components: input modalities, VLM backbones, and action prediction heads.

subsections.title: Input Modalities
subsections.description: Categorizes inputs into sensor observations, latent representations, language instructions, and vehicle state information.

subsections.title: Sensor Inputs
subsections.description: Describes raw data inputs like Visual Images and LiDAR Point Clouds.

subsections.title: Latent Representations
subsections.description: Covers intermediate representations like BEV Features and Occupancy Grids.

subsections.title: Language Inputs
subsections.description: Describes textual instructions or task descriptions used for grounding.

subsections.title: Vehicle State Information
subsections.description: Covers proprioceptive information like speed, acceleration, and steering angle.

subsections.title: VLM Backbone (F)
subsections.description: Explains the reasoning engine, distinguishing between single-system direct generation and dual-system guidance generation.

subsections.title: VLM for Direct Action Generation (Single-System)
subsections.description: Models where the VLM directly emits actions.

subsections.title: VLM for Guidance Generation (Dual-System)
subsections.description: Models where the VLM produces intermediate guidance for a downstream planner.

subsections.title: Action Prediction Head (H)
subsections.description: Categorizes action heads into Language Head, Regression, Trajectory Selection, and Trajectory Generation.

subsections.title: Action in Driving
subsections.description: Defines the output spaces: Discrete Trajectory, Continuous Trajectory, Direct Control, and Language Representations.

subsections.title: Discrete Trajectory Representations
subsections.description: Future path as a sequence of spatial waypoints.

subsections.title: Continuous Trajectory Representations
subsections.description: Motion parameterized as continuous functions over time.

subsections.title: Direct Control Representations
subsections.description: Low-level commands like steering, throttle, and brake.

subsections.title: Language Representations
subsections.description: Actions expressed as textual descriptions or tokens.

sections.title: Vision-Action Models
sections.description: Reviews the 'Past' era of End-to-End driving, categorizing methods into direct End-to-End models and World Models.

subsections.title: End-to-End Models for Autonomous Driving
subsections.description: Discusses models mapping sensors to actions, divided into Action-Only (IL/RL) and Perception-Action (BEV/Query) approaches.

subsections.title: Action-Only Model
subsections.description: One-stage formulation using Imitation Learning or Reinforcement Learning.

subsections.title: Perception-Action Model
subsections.description: Two-stage paradigm using Dense BEV-based or Sparse Query-based representations.

subsections.title: World Models for Autonomous Driving
subsections.description: Reviews models that predict scene evolution, categorized by prediction modality.

subsections.title: Image-Based World Model
subsections.description: Generates future frames using diffusion or autoregressive methods.

subsections.title: Occupancy-Based World Models
subsections.description: Predicts spatiotemporal occupancy grids rather than raw pixels.

subsections.title: Latent-Based World Models
subsections.description: Predicts dynamics in compressed latent space for efficiency.

subsections.title: Limitations of VA Compared to VLA
subsections.description: Highlights VA shortcomings: limited interpretability, weak generalization, lack of reasoning, and no language understanding.

sections.title: Vision-Language-Action Models
sections.description: The core 'Present' section proposing a taxonomy for VLA architectures: End-to-End VLA vs. Dual-System VLA.

subsections.title: End-to-End VLA for Autonomous Driving
subsections.description: Single models unifying perception, reasoning, and planning.

subsections.title: Textual Action Generator
subsections.description: Models producing Meta-Actions or Trajectory Waypoints in language space.

subsections.title: Numerical Action Generator
subsections.description: Models using additional action heads or action tokens to output numeric controls.

subsections.title: Dual-System VLA
subsections.description: Frameworks separating slow deliberation (VLM) from fast execution (Planner).

subsections.title: Explicit Action Guidance
subsections.description: VLM outputs structured actions (Meta-actions or Waypoints) refined by a planner.

subsections.title: Implicit Representations Transfer
subsections.description: VLM transfers reasoning via Knowledge Distillation or Multimodal Feature Fusion.

sections.title: Datasets & Benchmark
sections.description: Summarizes data resources and evaluation protocols for VLA research.

subsections.title: Datasets for VLA in Autonomous Driving
subsections.description: Contrasts traditional VA datasets with emerging VLA datasets containing language annotations.

subsections.title: Vision-Action Datasets
subsections.description: Traditional datasets like nuScenes and Waymo.

subsections.title: Vision-Language-Action Datasets
subsections.description: Datasets enriched with QA pairs, instructions, or rationales (e.g., DriveLM, NuInstruct).

subsections.title: Evaluation Metrics
subsections.description: Details how models are assessed based on output modality.

subsections.title: Trajectory-Based Action Evaluation
subsections.description: Open-loop (L2 error, collision rate) and Closed-loop (success rate, comfort) metrics.

subsections.title: Text-Based Action Evaluation
subsections.description: Linguistic quality metrics (BLEU, ROUGE) and reasoning consistency.

subsections.title: Quantitative Experiments & Analyses
subsections.description: Reviews quantitative benchmarks for evaluating VLA models across action prediction and planning accuracy.

sections.title: Challenges and Future Directions
sections.description: Discusses remaining hurdles such as robustness, interpretability, and instruction fidelity (Inferred from Outline/Intro).

sections.title: Conclusion
sections.description: Concluding remarks summarizing the paradigm shift and future outlook (Inferred from Outline/Intro).

structural_insights.organization_logic: The paper follows a 'Past-Present-Future' narrative arc. It establishes the mathematical and component foundations first (Sec 2), reviews the precursor technology (VA models, Sec 3), details the core subject (VLA models, Sec 4) with a specific taxonomy, and finally covers the enabling data/metrics (Sec 5).
structural_insights.transition_strategy: The transition is driven by the limitations of the previous generation. Section 3 ends by explicitly listing the limitations of VA models, which serves as the direct motivation for the VLA models introduced in Section 4. Section 4 is further divided by architectural complexity (End-to-End vs Dual-System).
structural_insights.depth_analysis: The outline is highly balanced. Section 3 (VA) and Section 4 (VLA) mirror each other in depth, both containing detailed taxonomies (Action-Only/Perception-Action vs Textual/Numerical). The Preliminary section (Sec 2) is unusually detailed for a survey, breaking down every component (Input, Backbone, Head), which provides a strong technical dictionary for the subsequent sections.
key_strengths: Clear historical narrative (Past/Present/Future) makes the evolution of technology easy to follow.
Rigorous taxonomy in Section 4 distinguishes between 'Textual' vs 'Numerical' outputs and 'Explicit' vs 'Implicit' guidance, which clarifies the vague landscape of VLA models.
Dedication of a specific section (2) to formalizing the mathematical formulation (Input/Backbone/Head) ensures consistent terminology throughout the survey.

outlines.paper_title: Tool Learning with Large Language Models: A Survey
outlines.paper_topic: Tool Learning with Large Language Models (LLMs)
outlines.outline_pattern: The survey follows a logical 'Why-How-Resources-Future' progression. It starts with the motivation ('Why'), moves to a detailed technical taxonomy based on a four-stage workflow ('How'), reviews experimental resources ('Benchmarks/Evaluation'), and concludes with open problems ('Challenges').

sections.title: Introduction
sections.description: Introduces the limitations of standard LLMs (hallucinations, outdated knowledge) and presents 'tool learning' as a solution. It outlines the survey's scope, focusing on why tool learning is beneficial and how it is implemented, and presents the paper's structural roadmap.

sections.title: Background
sections.description: Defines foundational concepts and terminology. It clarifies the definition of a 'Tool' (ranging from APIs to external programs) and 'Tool Learning' (the process of LLMs interacting with tools to solve complex tasks).

sections.title: Why Tool Learning?
sections.description: Analyzes the necessity of tool learning from two perspectives: the functional benefits of tool integration and the inherent benefits of the tool learning paradigm itself.

subsections.title: Knowledge Acquisition
subsections.description: Discusses how tools like search engines and databases allow LLMs to access up-to-date and structured external knowledge, mitigating hallucinations caused by parametric memory limitations.

subsections.title: Expertise Enhancement
subsections.description: Explains how specialized tools (calculators, Python interpreters, domain-specific models) bridge the gap in LLMs' specialized capabilities in math, coding, and sciences.

subsections.title: Automation and Efficiency
subsections.description: Describes how LLMs act as agents to execute actions in the real world, such as scheduling, email filtering, and shopping, thereby automating repetitive tasks.

subsections.title: Interaction Enhancement
subsections.description: Covers how tools extend LLM perception through multi-modal inputs (image/audio) and translation, improving intent understanding and user interaction.

subsections.title: Enhanced Interpretability and User Trust
subsections.description: Argues that tool usage makes the decision-making process transparent (showing steps and sources), reducing the 'black-box' nature of LLMs.

subsections.title: Improved Robustness and Adaptability
subsections.description: Suggests that relying on standardized tool interfaces makes LLMs less sensitive to prompt variations and more adaptable to new environments.

sections.title: How Tool Learning?
sections.description: The core technical section reviewing advancements across the tool learning workflow. It structures the review around four distinct stages: task planning, tool selection, tool calling, and response generation.

subsections.title: Overall Paradigm of Tool Learning
subsections.description: Outlines the four-stage workflow and distinguishes between two operational paradigms: 'One-step Task Solving' (planning without feedback) and 'Iterative Task Solving' (planning with feedback).

subsections.title: Task Planning
subsections.description: Reviews methods for decomposing user queries into sub-tasks and determining dependencies. Includes examples of GPT-4 planning.

subsections.title: Tuning-free Methods
subsections.description: Discusses prompt-based approaches like CoT, ReACT, and HuggingGPT that leverage innate LLM capabilities without weight updates.

subsections.title: Tuning-based Methods
subsections.description: Reviews methods that fine-tune LLMs (e.g., Toolformer, TaskMatrix.AI) to improve planning and API awareness.

subsections.title: Tool Selection
subsections.description: Analyzes how models choose appropriate tools from a library. Differentiates between retrieval-based and LLM-reasoning-based selection.

subsections.title: Retriever-based Tool Selection
subsections.description: Covers dense and sparse retrieval methods (TF-IDF, Sentence-Bert) used when the tool space is too large for the context window.

subsections.title: LLM-based Tool Selection
subsections.description: Reviews methods where the LLM selects tools from a provided list based on reasoning, categorized into tuning-free and tuning-based approaches.

subsections.title: Tool Calling
subsections.description: Examines how LLMs generate specific API calls and extract parameters from user queries, ensuring format compliance.

subsections.title: Tuning-free Methods
subsections.description: Methods using few-shot prompting or rule-based schemas to guide parameter extraction.

subsections.title: Tuning-based Methods
subsections.description: Methods like Gorilla and ToolkenGPT that fine-tune models to understand specific API documentation and token generation.

subsections.title: Response Generation
subsections.description: Discusses how tool outputs are synthesized into a final user response.

subsections.title: Direct Insertion Methods
subsections.description: Simple approaches where tool outputs directly replace placeholders in the generated text.

subsections.title: Information Integration Methods
subsections.description: Advanced methods where tool outputs are fed back into the context, allowing the LLM to synthesize and reason over the data.

sections.title: Benchmarks, Toolkits, and Evaluation
sections.description: Summarizes the ecosystem for validating tool learning, including datasets, software frameworks, and evaluation metrics.

subsections.title: Benchmarks
subsections.description: Categorizes benchmarks into 'General' (e.g., ToolBench, API-Bank) covering multiple stages, and 'Other' (specific to safety, robustness, or multi-modal tasks).

subsections.title: Toolkits
subsections.description: Lists open-source frameworks like LangChain, Auto-GPT, and BMTools that facilitate the development of tool-augmented LLMs.

subsections.title: Evaluation
subsections.description: Details specific metrics for each stage: Task Planning (pass rate), Tool Selection (Recall, NDCG), Tool Calling (parameter consistency), and Response Generation (BLEU, ROUGE).

sections.title: Challenges and Future Directions
sections.description: Identifies critical bottlenecks in the field and proposes research directions.

subsections.title: High Latency in Tool Learning
subsections.description: Discusses the performance trade-offs and the need for lower latency in real-time interactions.

subsections.title: Rigorous and Comprehensive Evaluation
subsections.description: Highlights the lack of standardized, cost-effective evaluation metrics beyond simple pass rates.

subsections.title: Comprehensive and Accessible Tools
subsections.description: Notes the limitation of current toolsets (often scraped or limited APIs) and the need for higher quality, diverse tool libraries.

subsections.title: Safe and Robust Tool Learning
subsections.description: Addresses security risks, including injection attacks and the robustness of models against noisy inputs.

subsections.title: Unified Tool Learning Framework
subsections.description: Calls for a standardized framework that integrates all four stages (planning, selection, calling, generation) rather than fragmented solutions.

subsections.title: Real-Word Benchmark for Tool Learning
subsections.description: Criticizes current benchmarks for relying on LLM-generated queries and calls for datasets based on real user behavior.

subsections.title: Tool Learning with Multi-Modal
subsections.description: Suggests expanding beyond text-based tools to include visual, audio, and video processing capabilities.

sections.title: Conclusion
sections.description: Summarizes the key findings of the survey. (Note: The specific content of this section is truncated in the provided PDF text, but the section is explicitly listed in the Introduction's roadmap).

structural_insights.organization_logic: The paper uses a 'Process-Oriented' taxonomy. Instead of grouping papers by model architecture or date, it groups them by the stage of the tool-use workflow (Planning -> Selection -> Calling -> Generation). This is highly effective for engineering implementation.
structural_insights.transition_strategy: The paper transitions from the abstract 'Why' to the concrete 'How'. Within the 'How' section, it follows the chronological execution path of an agent. It then moves from methods to evaluation (Benchmarks), and finally to open problems.
structural_insights.depth_analysis: The 'How Tool Learning' section (Section 4) is the deepest, containing multiple layers of nesting (Stage -> Paradigm -> Method Type). This indicates the paper is technically focused on methodology. The 'Why' section is also surprisingly detailed, providing a strong theoretical grounding.
key_strengths: Clear taxonomy based on the execution workflow (4 stages) makes it easy for developers to map components.
Consistent distinction between 'Tuning-free' (prompting) and 'Tuning-based' (fine-tuning) methods across all stages.
Comprehensive categorization of benchmarks by their focus (specific stages vs. general).
Inclusion of concrete GPT-4 examples for each stage helps visualize the abstract concepts.
